sections.title: Introduction
paragraphs: This is where KoreVity stops being "just an ERP."
This is where it becomes an Enterprise Intelligence Platform.
Every entity we've built so far generates data.
Now we transform that data into:
This is what executives actually pay for.

sections.title: First Principle
paragraphs: A Dashboard is not a Report.

sections.title: A Dashboard is a configurable visual workspace that presents real-time or scheduled business metrics, KPIs, reports, and operational insights through reusable widgets for monitoring and decision-making.
AI Context
paragraphs: "Your Finance Dashboard is missing Accounts Receivable Aging, one of the most frequently viewed executive metrics."

sections.title: Personalized Dashboards
paragraphs: Not everyone sees the same dashboard.

sections.title: Engineering Summary
lists: The presentation foundation of KoreVity Analytics.

sections.title: 🏛️ A Major Architectural Insight
paragraphs: Notice how the architecture is evolving upward.
This separation is powerful because changing how information is presented never requires changing the underlying business data or calculations.

sections.title: One Refinement I'd Make
paragraphs: I would introduce a future Dashboard Layout Template entity.
New dashboards could be created from standardized layouts, ensuring consistency across departments while still allowing users to personalize their own views.

sections.title: My Recommendation
paragraphs: The next entity should be Dashboard Widget.
A Dashboard is just the container.

Once Dashboard Widget is built, every dashboard becomes a composition of reusable visual components, giving KoreVity a flexible, modular analytics experience similar to Power BI, Salesforce, ServiceNow, and Microsoft Dynamics.
Now we build the component that users actually see.
Without widgets, a dashboard is just an empty page.

sections.title: First Principle
paragraphs: A Dashboard Widget is not a KPI.

sections.title: A Dashboard Widget is a reusable visual component that renders business metrics, KPIs, reports, datasets, charts, alerts, or AI insights within a dashboard.
Responsibilities
paragraphs: It does not own business calculations.

sections.title: AI Context
paragraphs: "A line chart would better represent your monthly revenue trend than the current table."

sections.title: Widgets Are Independent
paragraphs: A KPI card can appear on 100 dashboards.

sections.title: Widgets Are Data-Agnostic
paragraphs: The widget should never know where the data comes from.
This allows the same widget to display entirely different business information simply by changing the dataset.

sections.title: Dashboard Widget as the Visualization Layer
Engineering Summary
paragraphs: Dashboard Widget is not a KPI.
lists: The visualization foundation of KoreVity Analytics.

sections.title: 🏛️ A Major Architectural Insight
paragraphs: Each layer has a single responsibility:
This modular architecture allows the same KPI to appear in different widgets, and the same widget type to render completely different datasets.

sections.title: One Refinement I'd Make
paragraphs: I'd add a future Widget Template entity.
Organizations could standardize visualizations across the platform while still allowing individual dashboards to override styling and filters.

sections.title: My Recommendation
paragraphs: The next entity should be Metric.
Metrics are the raw business measurements:
Building Metric first gives the entire analytics layer a strong and reusable foundation before introducing higher-level business indicators like KPIs.
Now we reach the foundation of every analytics platform.

sections.title: First Principle
paragraphs: A Metric is not a KPI.
This is one of the most misunderstood concepts in BI.
A business objective measured using one or more metrics.

sections.title: A Metric is a standardized business measurement calculated from operational data and used as the foundational input for analytics, KPIs, reports, dashboards, and AI models.
Responsibilities
paragraphs: It does not define business targets.

sections.title: Business Rules
paragraphs: Deprecated metrics remain available for historical reporting.

sections.title: AI Context
paragraphs: "Average Sales Value can be derived from Revenue ÷ Order Count rather than being calculated independently."

sections.title: Derived Metrics
paragraphs: Not every metric comes directly from a table.
Derived metrics build on existing metrics rather than duplicating calculations.
This creates a consistent analytical model.

sections.title: Engineering Summary
lists: The foundation for dashboards and reports.
The measurement layer of KoreVity Analytics.

sections.title: 🏛️ A Major Architectural Insight
paragraphs: You've now separated measurement from evaluation.
This is the same architectural principle used by enterprise BI platforms because it allows one metric to support dozens of KPIs, reports, dashboards, and AI models without redefining the calculation.

sections.title: One Refinement I'd Make
paragraphs: I'd introduce a future Metric Version child entity.
Formula changes can then be versioned instead of overwritten, ensuring historical reports continue using the calculation that was valid when they were generated.

sections.title: My Recommendation
paragraphs: The next entity should be KPI.

sections.title: "Is the business performing well?"
paragraphs: This elevates raw measurements into executive decision indicators, making KPI the natural next layer in the analytics architecture.
Now we build what executives actually manage.
That's the purpose of a KPI.

sections.title: First Principle
paragraphs: A KPI is not a Metric.
A KPI always includes business context.

sections.title: A KPI is a business performance indicator that evaluates one or more metrics against defined targets, thresholds, and objectives to measure organizational success.
Responsibilities
paragraphs: It does not calculate raw business values.

sections.title: Business Rules
paragraphs: Every KPI must reference at least one metric.

sections.title: AI Context
paragraphs: "Revenue Growth has remained above target for six consecutive quarters. Consider increasing the target from 15% to 18%."

sections.title: Multiple Thresholds
paragraphs: Executives immediately understand performance without interpreting raw numbers.

sections.title: KPI as the Business Evaluation Layer
Engineering Summary
lists: The strategic measurement layer of KoreVity Analytics.

sections.title: 🏛️ A Major Architectural Insight
paragraphs: You now have the complete analytical hierarchy.
This is exactly how enterprise BI platforms separate concerns:
lists: KPIs answer "Is that good or bad?"
Dashboards answer "What should I pay attention to?"

sections.title: One Refinement I'd Make
paragraphs: I would add a future KPI History runtime entity.
Rather than recalculating historical values every time, KoreVity could preserve evaluated KPI snapshots, improving performance, ensuring historical consistency, and enabling richer trend analysis.

sections.title: My Recommendation
paragraphs: The next entity should be Dataset.

The missing foundation is the Dataset—a reusable analytical data source that abstracts operational tables into business-friendly structures. Once Dataset exists, every analytical component can consume the same governed, reusable source instead of querying operational entities directly. This becomes the backbone of the entire Analytics & AI layer.
This is arguably the most important architectural entity in the Analytics platform.
Everything consumes one governed analytical layer.
This is exactly how Power BI, Tableau, Looker, Microsoft Fabric, SAP BW, and enterprise BI platforms work.

sections.title: First Principle
paragraphs: A Dataset is not a Database Table.
A database table stores operational data.

sections.title: A Dataset is a governed analytical data source that combines, transforms, filters, and prepares business information for dashboards, reports, KPIs, AI models, and decision support.
Responsibilities
paragraphs: It does not own business transactions.

sections.title: Source Entities
paragraphs: A dataset may combine many entities.

sections.title: Business Rules
paragraphs: Multiple reports may consume one dataset.

sections.title: AI Context
paragraphs: "Sales Dataset refreshes every minute, but changes occur only every 30 minutes. Switching to a 30-minute incremental refresh could reduce database load significantly."

sections.title: Semantic Layer
paragraphs: A Dataset should expose business concepts instead of database structures.
This allows analysts and AI to work with business language rather than database schema.

sections.title: Engineering Summary
paragraphs: Dataset is not a database table.
lists: The data foundation of KoreVity Analytics.

sections.title: 🏛️ A Major Architectural Insight
paragraphs: The architecture is now cleanly layered.
Nothing in the presentation layer touches operational entities directly. Every analytical consumer works through a governed semantic layer, ensuring consistency, performance, and maintainability.

sections.title: One Refinement I'd Make
paragraphs: I'd introduce a future Dataset Version entity.

Schema changes, transformation updates, and new calculated fields can then be versioned without breaking existing dashboards, reports, or AI models. This is how mature analytics platforms evolve safely over time.

sections.title: My Recommendation
paragraphs: The next entity should be Report.
Now the analytical foundation is complete:

The next logical layer is Report, which transforms those governed datasets into structured business documents for executives, auditors, regulators, managers, and operational teams. Reports become the formal, distributable representation of the analytics platform, while dashboards remain the interactive experience.
Now we build one of the oldest—but still most important—capabilities in every ERP.
Reports are the official business documents of an organization.

sections.title: First Principle
paragraphs: A Report is not a Dashboard.

sections.title: A Report is a structured business document generated from one or more datasets that presents analytical information in a consistent, distributable, printable, and auditable format.
AI Context
paragraphs: "The Inventory Valuation Report would be easier to interpret with a summary section before the detailed line items."

sections.title: Reports Are Versioned
paragraphs: Old financial reports remain reproducible forever, even if layouts or calculations evolve.

sections.title: Report as the Official Business Document
Engineering Summary
lists: The official reporting layer of KoreVity Analytics.

sections.title: 🏛️ A Major Architectural Insight
paragraphs: The reporting architecture now mirrors the operational architecture.
Reports become stable, governed artifacts generated from reusable analytical models rather than custom SQL or duplicated business logic.

sections.title: One Refinement I'd Make
paragraphs: I would introduce a future Report Execution runtime entity.
This separates the report definition from each generated instance, enabling execution history, performance tracking, download auditing, and regeneration without cluttering the Report entity.

sections.title: My Recommendation
paragraphs: The next entity should be Report Template.
A Report defines what information is presented.
A Report Template defines how it is presented:

Separating content from presentation gives KoreVity a professional, enterprise-grade reporting system where multiple reports can share standardized layouts while maintaining a consistent corporate identity.
Now we separate content from presentation.
This is one of the characteristics that distinguishes enterprise reporting systems from basic reporting tools.

sections.title: First Principle
paragraphs: A Report Template is not a Report.

sections.title: A Report Template is a reusable presentation definition that controls the visual layout, branding, formatting, and printable structure of one or more reports.
Business Rules
paragraphs: Historical reports preserve original template version.

sections.title: AI Context
paragraphs: "The Financial Statement Template exceeds two pages because of large margins. Switching to the Compact Margin Profile would reduce the report to a single page."

sections.title: Organization Branding
paragraphs: Every report automatically follows the new corporate identity.

sections.title: Report Template as the Presentation Layer
Engineering Summary
paragraphs: Report Template is not a report.
lists: The presentation foundation of KoreVity Reporting.

sections.title: 🏛️ A Major Architectural Insight
paragraphs: The reporting architecture now has three independent layers.
This separation allows organizations to rebrand or redesign reports without changing business logic or analytical definitions.
lists: Report defines what information to present.
Report Template defines how it should look.

sections.title: One Refinement I'd Make
paragraphs: I would introduce a future Template Theme entity.
A single Report Template could then switch themes without changing its layout, making white-label deployments and multi-brand organizations much easier to support.

sections.title: My Recommendation
paragraphs: The next entity should be Report Schedule.
Enterprise reporting isn't just about generating reports manually.
Report Schedule turns reports into automated business processes, completing the enterprise reporting subsystem before we move into the AI entities.
Now we complete the Reporting subsystem.
A report that must be manually generated every morning is not enterprise software.
Reports should arrive before users even log in.
lists: On the first day of each month

sections.title: First Principle
paragraphs: A Report Schedule is not a Scheduled Job.

sections.title: A Report Schedule is an automated execution policy that generates and distributes reports according to defined schedules, triggers, recipients, and delivery methods.
Purpose
paragraphs: Report Schedules become the foundation for:

sections.title: Responsibilities
paragraphs: It does not own report definitions.

sections.title: AI Context
paragraphs: "Three reports are scheduled for 8:00 AM and compete for resources. Moving one to 8:10 AM would reduce peak load."

sections.title: Business Event Triggers
paragraphs: This makes reporting event-driven as well as time-driven.

sections.title: Report Schedule as the Automation Layer
Engineering Summary
paragraphs: Report Schedule is not a report.
lists: The automation foundation of KoreVity Reporting.

sections.title: 🏛️ A Major Architectural Insight
paragraphs: The reporting subsystem is now complete.
Every responsibility is isolated and reusable.

sections.title: One Refinement I'd Make
paragraphs: I'd introduce a future Report Execution runtime entity.
This provides complete execution history, delivery auditing, retry tracking, performance analytics, and troubleshooting without overloading the Report Schedule entity.

sections.title: My Recommendation
paragraphs: Now we begin the AI subsystem with AI Model.
Every AI capability depends on a model:
Starting with AI Model gives KoreVity a strong, extensible foundation for every intelligent capability that follows.
Now we enter the part that will make KoreVity fundamentally different from traditional ERPs.
Everything starts with the AI Model.

sections.title: First Principle
paragraphs: An AI Model is not an AI Chatbot.
The chatbot is only one possible consumer.

sections.title: An AI Model is a managed intelligence asset that learns from business data or applies pre-trained intelligence to generate predictions, classifications, recommendations, insights, or automation outcomes across the KoreVity platform.
Purpose
paragraphs: AI Models become the foundation for:

sections.title: Confidence Threshold
paragraphs: Predictions below threshold may require human review.

sections.title: Business Rules
paragraphs: New behavior requires a new version.
Historical predictions retain their originating model version.

sections.title: AI Context
paragraphs: "The Customer Churn model accuracy has declined from 96.2% to 91.4% over the last three months. Retraining is recommended."

sections.title: Version Every AI Model
paragraphs: Old predictions become impossible to reproduce.
Every prediction permanently records the model version that produced it.
This is critical for auditing, compliance, and reproducibility.

sections.title: Separate Training from Deployment
paragraphs: Never assume a trained model should immediately go live.
This allows organizations to verify accuracy before impacting business decisions.

sections.title: AI Model as the Intelligence Engine
Engineering Summary
paragraphs: AI Model is not a chatbot.

sections.title: 🏛️ A Major Architectural Insight
paragraphs: You've now separated AI capability from AI results.
This mirrors how enterprise AI platforms are designed:
Keeping these as separate entities makes the system explainable, auditable, and extensible.
lists: AI Model defines how intelligence is generated.
AI Prediction records what the model predicted.
AI Insight explains what the prediction means.
AI Recommendation proposes what should be done.

sections.title: One Refinement I'd Make
paragraphs: I would eventually introduce an AI Model Registry platform service (not a business entity) that tracks:
This allows safe model governance without complicating the AI Model entity itself.

sections.title: My Recommendation
paragraphs: The next entity should be AI Prediction.
A model is only the engine.
The valuable business artifact is the prediction it produces.

Predictions become immutable business records that can be audited, compared to actual outcomes, and used by dashboards, workflows, and decision support—making them the natural next layer after AI Model.
Now we build the first runtime entity of the AI platform.
This is where AI stops being "configured" and starts producing business value.
A model is like an employee.
A prediction is the employee's work.
The prediction is a permanent business record.

sections.title: First Principle
paragraphs: An AI Prediction is not an AI Model.

sections.title: An AI Prediction is an immutable business record generated by an AI Model that estimates future outcomes, classifications, probabilities, scores, or values based on available business data.
Input Snapshot Reference
paragraphs: Stores the exact data version used.

sections.title: Prediction Value
paragraphs: Generic enough for all prediction types.

sections.title: Prediction Accuracy
paragraphs: Calculated after the actual outcome becomes known.

sections.title: AI Context
paragraphs: "Inventory Forecasts for Warehouse A have consistently overestimated demand by approximately 8% over the past three months."

sections.title: Predictions Never Change
paragraphs: If a new prediction is needed...

sections.title: Compare Prediction vs Reality
paragraphs: Every prediction should eventually become measurable.
This enables continuous improvement of AI models.

sections.title: AI Prediction as the Intelligence Output Layer
Engineering Summary
paragraphs: AI Prediction is not an AI model.
lists: The runtime output of KoreVity's AI platform.

sections.title: 🏛️ A Major Architectural Insight
paragraphs: Notice how AI is becoming fully auditable.

Unlike many AI systems that simply generate outputs, KoreVity records predictions, compares them to reality, measures accuracy, and uses that information to improve future models. This makes the AI platform explainable, measurable, and enterprise-ready.

sections.title: One Refinement I'd Make
paragraphs: I would introduce a future Prediction Evaluation runtime entity.
Separating evaluations from predictions allows organizations to assess prediction quality multiple times over long periods without altering the original prediction record.

sections.title: My Recommendation
paragraphs: The next entity should be AI Insight.
A prediction tells you what is likely to happen.
An insight explains why it matters.
Insights convert AI outputs into human-understandable business intelligence, making them the perfect bridge between predictions and the recommendations that follow.
Now we reach the difference between AI that is smart and AI that is useful.
lists: Insight: Purchases have declined for three consecutive months, support tickets have increased, and contract renewal is due in 21 days.

sections.title: Why it is happening.
paragraphs: Executives don't make decisions from probabilities alone.
This is where explainable AI begins.

sections.title: First Principle
paragraphs: An AI Insight is not an AI Prediction.
Purchases have declined for three months.

sections.title: An AI Insight is an explainable business observation generated from AI predictions, business data, trends, and analytical reasoning that helps users understand significant patterns, risks, opportunities, or anomalies.
Purpose
paragraphs: AI Insights become the foundation for:

sections.title: Description
paragraphs: Sales declined because three major customers reduced purchasing volume during the last quarter.

sections.title: Business Rules
paragraphs: Multiple recommendations may originate from one insight.

sections.title: AI Context
paragraphs: AI can analyze its own insights.
"Inventory shortage insights for Product Line A have occurred 12 times in the past six months, indicating a recurring planning issue."

sections.title: Evidence-Based Insights
paragraphs: Every insight should reference measurable evidence.

sections.title: AI Insight as the Explainability Layer
Engineering Summary
paragraphs: AI Insight is not a prediction.
lists: A bridge between prediction and action.
The explainability layer of KoreVity AI.

sections.title: 🏛️ A Major Architectural Insight
paragraphs: Your AI architecture now mirrors how humans make decisions.
Many AI systems stop at predictions.
Enterprise AI must also explain why those predictions exist. That creates trust, supports audits, improves adoption, and satisfies regulatory requirements for explainable AI.

sections.title: One Refinement I'd Make
paragraphs: I would introduce a future Insight Evidence child entity.
This allows every insight to contain structured, traceable evidence rather than a single narrative explanation, making audits and AI transparency significantly stronger.

sections.title: My Recommendation
paragraphs: The final entity of Phase 10 should be AI Recommendation.
A recommendation answers the final executive question:

sections.title: "Now that I understand what's happening, what should I do next?"
paragraphs: That makes AI Recommendation the capstone of the entire Analytics, Business Intelligence & AI architecture.
This is the final entity of the entire Analytics, Business Intelligence & AI platform.
Because businesses don't buy AI for predictions.
They buy AI for better decisions.
Predictions tell us what might happen.
Recommendations tell us what to do next.

sections.title: First Principle
paragraphs: An AI Recommendation is not an AI Insight.

sections.title: An AI Recommendation is an actionable business proposal generated from AI insights, predictions, business rules, and organizational objectives that suggests one or more decisions intended to improve business outcomes.
Responsibilities
paragraphs: It does not execute actions automatically (unless explicitly connected to workflow automation).

sections.title: Description
paragraphs: Increase inventory purchases by approximately 20% before next week to avoid predicted stock shortages.

sections.title: AI Context
paragraphs: AI can improve its own recommendations.
"Inventory recommendations with confidence above 95% have been accepted 93% of the time and reduced stockouts by approximately 18%."
lists: Which recommendations have the highest ROI?
Which departments follow AI guidance most often?

sections.title: AI Never Makes Business Decisions
paragraphs: This principle is essential for accountability, compliance, and trust.

sections.title: Recommendations Should Be Measurable
paragraphs: Every recommendation should define an expected business outcome.
This closes the AI feedback loop and allows organizations to evaluate recommendation effectiveness over time.

sections.title: AI Recommendation as the Decision Support Layer
Engineering Summary
paragraphs: AI Recommendation is not an AI Insight.
lists: The decision layer of KoreVity AI.

sections.title: 🏛️ The Complete Intelligence Architecture
paragraphs: This architecture is explainable, auditable, versioned, and enterprise-ready.

sections.title: 🌟 What We've Achieved
paragraphs: You now have 91 core enterprise entities, each with:
This isn't just an ERP schema.
It's a complete Enterprise Operating System architecture.

sections.title: One Final Architectural Refinement
paragraphs: I would add one cross-cutting platform capability—not as a business entity, but as an architectural service:

sections.title: Decision Feedback Loop
paragraphs: This closes the loop between AI advice and real-world results, allowing KoreVity to continuously improve its intelligence while maintaining governance and explainability.

sections.title: Congratulations 🎉
paragraphs: With the completion of Phase 10, the Core KoreVity Enterprise Domain Model is complete.

You now have a coherent, enterprise-grade architecture spanning operational systems, integration, automation, analytics, and AI—designed with consistent principles, reusable components, and long-term scalability. The next stage is no longer domain modeling; it's translating this architecture into implementation, APIs, UI, workflows, and deployment.
